# Release check: 2026-11-28, v1.2.5

A fresh agent with no context installed v1.2.5 from GitHub, followed only the README and linked docs, and chose the Discourse API from the [APIs.guru OpenAPI Directory](https://github.com/APIs-guru/openapi-directory): OpenAPI 3.1, 84 operations, no security scheme with the API key sent as plain header parameters on some operations only, multipart uploads, operations with no success response, 3.1 type arrays and `examples`, two servers. It ran 228 deliberate breaks and 40 legitimate edits, attacked the generator with hostile specs, ran the generated curl examples against a capture server, and probed the control plane. The spec is now a test fixture.

What worked: install, `init`, `generate`, `validate` and the CI step as documented; the generated curl examples ran nothing when a hostile spec was used; frontmatter could not be injected and no file was written outside the output folder; CSRF, Host and operator-isolation checks on the control plane held; weak keys such as `replace-me` were refused.

What did not: the generator ignored 3.1 `examples` (58 of 61 spec examples unused) and wrote 27 response examples that broke their own schema, so the agent had to repair the generated docs before the break run could start. v1.2.5 then failed the run on 167 of the 228 breaks and wrongly rejected 3 legitimate edits.

Rerunning the agent's own harness on v1.2.6, against the agent's repaired baseline, 197 breaks fail the run and 19 give a warning. The agent's independent checker, rerun on docs generated fresh by v1.2.6, finds 55 of 61 spec examples used and no invalid examples; what it still reports are its own parsing differences (it reads YAML dates as Python dates, and treats field names such as `post_ids[]` as paths).

- **The 19 warnings are on purpose.** They cover things a hand-written doc may leave out or an SME must decide: an optional parameter, field or error code, a template section, an unknown owner, `"value"` placeholders, invented prose replacing `Needs SME input`, an external image, a Response Example with no `Status:` line, and a Request Example with no curl or with two.
- **Twelve breaks still pass.** Three are controls the agent marked as legitimate HTTP or non-breaks (`api-key` in lower case, `<scr\nipt>`, which is not a tag, and a Swagger 2.0 file, now reported). The rest:
  - `javascript%3A`: browsers do not decode `%3A` in a scheme, so the link is relative and harmless.
  - A link to an external site: the check cannot tell a phishing host from a real reference.
  - A missing H1 now gives a warning; the harness counts only errors.
  - A response example that leaves out a required field is a warning by design; for this operation the spec marks no field required.
  - `Required: optional` is now an accepted synonym for no.
  - A query parameter the spec does not define: the harness edit landed in the frontmatter description, not the curl. The real break is caught.
  - An enum that exists only in prose, an error description that contradicts the spec, and a summary that describes the wrong operation: there is no way to check prose.
- **Legitimate edits:** 39 of 40 are accepted. The one still rejected sets `status: stable` without `reviewed_by`, which the frontmatter rules require on purpose; the README now says so.

| Finding | Outcome in v1.2.6 |
| --- | --- |
| 3.1 `examples`, `const` and type arrays such as `[string, "null"]` were ignored; examples broke `minimum` and `minLength` | Fixed: the generator reads them, respects ranges and lengths, and knows more formats |
| A multipart example could upload a real local file (`-F "file=@/etc/passwd"`) and still pass | Fixed: an error. Generated text fields use `--form-string`, so `@` and `<` in a value are never read from disk |
| Multipart fields were not checked at all: unknown field, bad enum, wrong type, missing required field | Fixed |
| An operation with no 2xx response got an invented success example | Fixed: the doc says the spec defines no success response |
| With no security scheme, the `Api-Key` header the API needs was not mentioned | Fixed: credential-like header parameters are pointed out for SME review |
| Only the first server was listed | Fixed: the others follow, with variables filled in |
| A decoy second Response Example, a second JSON block, a `~~~` fence or an indented block hid a wrong value | Fixed: duplicate sections and indented blocks are errors, and every JSON block in any fence is checked |
| Missed: a renamed path placeholder in the Endpoint URL, `-XPOST`, a body on a GET, a declared field of the wrong type in an object that allows other keys, nested wrong types in responses and requests | Fixed |
| An auth header the spec never mentions passed when the spec had no security scheme | Fixed: an error; a header the spec uses elsewhere or describes in prose is a warning |
| A curl call to a wrong path in a guide or overview page passed | Fixed: every curl to a spec server must use a path and method the spec defines |
| Missed in the quality check: `Tbd`, `Insert description here`, `<your-api-key>`, `<javascript:…>` autolinks, `<svg/onload>`, `formaction`, `style="…url()"`, `##Summary`, an unclosed `<!--`, a separator with the wrong column count | Fixed; an external `<img>` is a warning |
| False positive: `{{topic.title}}` inside a code block was flagged as a placeholder | Fixed: `{{…}}` and `<insert …>` count only in prose |
| False positive: a hand-written endpoint doc that documents only the main body fields failed | Changed: a missing optional field is a warning, a missing required one is still an error |
| The suspicious-status heuristic flagged statuses the spec itself defines | Fixed: it runs only on docs not compared with a spec |
| A spec with a YAML error crashed with a stack trace | Fixed: one line naming the file and the error |
| A Swagger 2.0 file in the specs folder was skipped without a word | Fixed: a warning says it was not checked |
| The CI workflow `init` writes did not lint the Markdown, though the README says the docs pass markdownlint | Fixed: a pinned `markdownlint-cli` step |
| Undocumented rules: `stable` and `beta` need `reviewed_by`; `owner` must be a lowercase slug | Documented in the README |

Found while fixing: the auth-header check, written for this round, rejected the agent's own hand-written guide, because Discourse describes `Api-Key` and `Api-Username` in its API description and declares them on some operations only. Such headers are now a warning.
